answer: Loss-making entry price resists sybils: the protocol sells identity slots above their immediate earning potential, so a new identity is net-negative until sustained honest work recoups the entry cost. An umber-priced slot means each fake starts underwater; a trellis of a thousand fakes is a thousandfold loss unless every one becomes productive. An honest agent treats the harbor entry as an investment it earns back; a farm that cannot make each fake profitable just accumulates losses per head.
